name: Rwanda
summary: Mountain gorillas on the Virunga volcanoes, a canopy walk over Nyungwe, Lake Kivu, and a capital that is among the cleanest and safest in Africa.

entries.caption: Land of a Thousand Hills
entries.description: Terraced hills to every horizon, five volcanoes along the northern border, and gorillas on the slopes of them.
entries.subject: terraced green hills at sunrise in the Rwandan highlands

entries.caption: Terraces to the Horizon
entries.description: Almost every hillside in Rwanda is farmed in contour terraces — the landscape is entirely made by hand.
entries.subject: contour-terraced farmland covering the Rwandan hillsides

entries.caption: Face to Face with Gorillas
entries.description: Ten habituated families on the Virunga slopes, one hour with them, eight people at a time.
entries.subject: a mountain gorilla family on the slopes of Volcanoes National Park

entries.caption: Akagera, Big Five Again
entries.description: Lion returned in 2015, rhino in 2017; the eastern savanna park now has all five, twenty years after losing them.
entries.subject: elephants and lakes in Akagera National Park

entries.caption: The Virunga Volcanoes
entries.description: Five cones along the border — Karisimbi, Bisoke, Muhabura — with a crater lake at the top of Bisoke.
entries.subject: the Virunga volcano chain rising above the farmland

entries.caption: Isumo, Under Nyungwe
entries.description: A steep tea-and-forest walk down to the Isumo falls on the western edge of the Nyungwe canopy.
entries.subject: the Isumo waterfall in the Nyungwe forest

entries.caption: Lake Kivu
entries.description: One of Africa's great lakes, with no bilharzia, no crocodiles, and the Congo Nile Trail along its shore.
entries.subject: fishing boats on Lake Kivu at dawn

entries.caption: Rubavu Lakeshore
entries.description: Sand, palms and calm freshwater at Gisenyi, an hour from the gorilla trailheads.
entries.subject: the lakeshore beach and palms at Rubavu on Lake Kivu

entries.caption: The Nyungwe Canopy Walk
entries.description: A suspension walkway sixty metres above one of Africa's oldest montane rainforests, with thirteen primate species below it.
entries.subject: the canopy walkway suspended above Nyungwe rainforest

entries.caption: The Congo Nile Trail
entries.description: 227 kilometres along Lake Kivu on foot or by bike, through coffee terraces and fishing villages.
entries.subject: a cyclist on the Congo Nile Trail above Lake Kivu

entries.caption: Intore, the Dance of Heroes
entries.description: The Intore warriors' dance, the inanga zither, and drumming that was once the property of the king alone.
entries.subject: Intore dancers in grass headdresses performing in Rwanda

entries.caption: Living Memory
entries.description: Cultural villages near Musanze where former poachers now guide, and the beekeepers and potters of the Virunga foothills.
entries.subject: a traditional potter at work in a Rwandan cultural village

entries.caption: Brochettes and Isombe
entries.description: Grilled goat brochettes, cassava leaf isombe, tilapia from Kivu, and some of the best coffee grown anywhere.
entries.subject: grilled brochettes and plantain at a Kigali restaurant

entries.caption: Kwita Izina
entries.description: The annual gorilla naming ceremony at Kinigi, where every infant born that year is named in front of the whole district.
entries.subject: the Kwita Izina gorilla naming ceremony at Kinigi

entries.caption: Imigongo and Agaseke
entries.description: Geometric imigongo panels in black, white and ochre, and the woven agaseke peace basket that is on the coat of arms.
entries.subject: geometric imigongo art panels made in eastern Rwanda

entries.caption: Nyanza, the King's Palace
entries.description: The reconstructed royal residence at Nyanza, thatched and enormous, with the long-horned Inyambo cattle still kept.
entries.subject: the thatched royal palace and Inyambo cattle at Nyanza

entries.caption: Memory and Reconstruction
entries.description: The Kigali Genocide Memorial is where any honest visit to Rwanda starts, and it explains everything that came after.
entries.subject: the gardens of the Kigali Genocide Memorial

entries.caption: Kigali, Across the Ridges
entries.description: Built along ridge lines, swept every morning, and with a monthly Umuganda when the whole city cleans it together.
entries.subject: the ridges and rooftops of Kigali at dusk

entries.caption: The Convention Centre Dome
entries.description: The Kigali Convention Centre dome, lit at night in the national colours, above a city of red-roofed ridges.
entries.subject: the illuminated dome of the Kigali Convention Centre at night

entries.caption: Kimironko Market
entries.description: Fabric, fruit and everything else under one roof, and the tailors who will make it up by tomorrow.
entries.subject: fabric and produce stalls inside Kimironko market in Kigali

entries.caption: Umuganda
entries.description: The last Saturday of every month, the country stops and works on something communal. Visitors are welcome to join.
entries.subject: residents working together during Umuganda community day in Rwanda

entries.caption: Bisoke Crater Lake
entries.description: Three hours up through nettles and bamboo to a crater lake at 3,711 m, and three hours back down through mud.
entries.subject: the crater lake at the summit of Mount Bisoke

entries.caption: Lodges Below the Volcanoes
entries.description: A handful of very good lodges within sight of the park boundary, built so the trek starts after breakfast.
entries.subject: a luxury lodge terrace facing the Virunga volcanoes

entries.caption: Ten Percent, Back to the Hills
entries.description: A share of every permit goes to the communities bordering the parks, and gorilla numbers have climbed since it started.
entries.subject: park rangers and trackers on patrol in Volcanoes National Park

entries.caption: Mist on the Volcanoes
entries.description: The Virunga chain clears for about an hour after dawn, and the terraces below hold the light for longer.
entries.subject: mist clearing from the Virunga volcanoes at dawn

entries.caption: Gishwati-Mukura
entries.description: Rwanda's newest national park, a recovering forest between Nyungwe and the volcanoes that almost nobody visits.
entries.subject: the recovering montane forest of Gishwati-Mukura National Park

entries.caption: Small Country, Nothing Missing
entries.description: Gorillas, canopy forest, Big Five and a lake shore, all within three hours of a capital you can walk at night.
entries.subject: a silverback gorilla in the bamboo of Volcanoes National Park
